input.rationale: Cite the successor receipt and fold its mechanism-isolating control into the current account: the identical 8193-entry replay that hangs at MaxAppendEntries=64 completes in 2 ms at MaxAppendEntries=1024, which attributes the stall to the batch count rather than the entry count or store state. Knowledge records gain the new receipt's case and result indices; the changed exposure is recorded in counterevidence and limitations rather than appended as a correction.

knowledge.statement: NewRaft() calls restoreFromCommittedLogs() synchronously, which clamps the store's staged commit index to the last log index, sets the commit index and calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs flushes a commitTuple batch to r.fsmMutateCh every MaxAppendEntries entries and once more for the remainder, and the only goroutine that reads fsmMutateCh (runFSM) is started after NewRaft returns.
knowledge.conditions: RestoreCommittedLogs=true and a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; no snapshot restored at or above the staged commit index.

knowledge.statement: For the captured code, the startup replay can enqueue at most 128 batches because fsmMutateCh is created with capacity 128 and its send in processLogs selects only on that send and on r.shutdownCh; with DefaultConfig MaxAppendEntries=64 this allows at most 8192 committed entries beyond the last snapshot, so 8193 or more replayed entries have no enabled progress path (no consumer exists and shutdownCh has no closer).
knowledge.conditions: RestoreCommittedLogs=true, DefaultConfig values, restart with staged commit index exceeding last snapshot index by more than 8192.

interpretations.rationale: Conclusion: violated. With RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, NewRaft does not complete a legal replay of already-committed log entries once the replay needs more than 128 FSM dispatch batches; the caller never receives the *Raft, so the node has no way to start, serve or shut down. This is a startup progress failure, not a decision-safety failure: no commit, vote or membership decision was observed to be wrong. Evidence. Receipt d61420dbc49a4072937b040aac55a51c (completed, tests_passed, exit 0): parsed index 1, seeded commit-tracking store with 8192 committed entries = exactly 128 batches at MaxAppendEntries=64, returned=true in 5 ms; parsed index 3, the retained state of a real single-node cluster that committed 8300 commands through the leader/commit/apply path and then snapshotted at index 8302 above the staged commit index, replay 0 batches, returned=true in 0 ms; parsed index 5, the same seeded store with 8193 entries = 129 batches, returned=false after 5000 ms with one newly blocked (*Raft).processLogs goroutine and one newly blocked (*Raft).restoreFromCommittedLogs goroutine; parsed index 7, the same real-cluster prefix without a snapshot, staged commit 8300 = 130 batches, returned=false after 5000 ms with the same two newly blocked goroutines. Successor receipt 87aea51bbd8a4b579f138f2c4986343a (completed, tests_passed, exit 0) reproduced all four outcomes (parsed indices 1, 3, 7, 9) and added parsed index 5: the identical 8193-entry store state that hangs at MaxAppendEntries=64, replayed as 9 batches with MaxAppendEntries=1024, returned=true in 2 ms. That comparison holds entry count, log content, staged commit index and snapshot state fixed and varies only the batch size, so the stall is attributable to the number of batches relative to the 128-slot channel rather than to log volume, snapshot handling, store state or the producing cluster; the goroutine match in both hanging cases localizes the block to processLogs invoked from restoreFromCommittedLogs. Mechanism from source: api.go:606 calls restoreFromCommittedLogs before any background goroutine exists; api.go:753 calls processLogs(commitIndex, nil); raft.go:1303-1313 sends each commitTuple batch into fsmMutateCh and selects only on that send and on r.shutdownCh; fsmMutateCh has capacity 128 (api.go:560); its only reader runFSM (fsm.go:241) is started at api.go:637 after NewRaft returns; api.go:1065 is the only closer of shutdownCh and is reachable only through a *Raft. After 128 successful sends the 129th send therefore has no producer and no possible closer, so the block is permanent rather than slow. Consequence under the exercised conditions: a node restarting with the documented RestoreCommittedLogs option and with more than 128*MaxAppendEntries committed entries beyond its last snapshot hangs inside NewRaft indefinitely while reporting no error.

knowledge.assertion: NewRaft calls restoreFromCommittedLogs synchronously and processLogs flushes batches into fsmMutateCh while runFSM starts only after NewRaft returns.
The startup replay can enqueue at most 128 batches, so with DefaultConfig 8193 or more replayed entries beyond the last snapshot have no enabled progress path.

counterevidence: RestoreCommittedLogs is not part of DefaultConfig (config.go:329-341 leaves it false), and with the option disabled restoreFromCommittedLogs returns immediately (api.go:725-727), so default-configured nodes cannot reach the blocked path.

A snapshot at or near the commit index removes the replay entirely: parsed index 3 in both receipts restarted the same 8300-commit real prefix with replay_batches=0 and returned NewRaft immediately, so snapshot cadence bounds exposure to this path.

A larger MaxAppendEntries moves the boundary: parsed index 5 of receipt 87aea51bbd8a4b579f138f2c4986343a completed the very state that hangs at the default batch size, so a deployment that raises MaxAppendEntries enough for 128*MaxAppendEntries to cover its snapshot lag does not encounter the block.

The trigger observations are 5000 ms observation windows, not infinite runs; permanence is claimed from the source-level absence of any consumer before NewRaft returns and from shutdownCh having no closer outside Shutdown on the returned *Raft, not from the timeout alone.
No incorrect commit, applied entry, vote or membership decision was observed in any case; the evidence contradicts only startup progress.
limitations: The boundary is 128*MaxAppendEntries committed entries beyond the last snapshot. Only two batch sizes were exercised (64, boundary 8192, blocked at 8193; 1024, 9 batches, returned); the 128-slot fsmMutateCh capacity itself is not configurable, and no case exercised a replay that lands exactly at 128 batches with a non-default batch size.

Parsed indices 1, 5 and 7 (successor) seed the commit-tracking store directly; only the snapshot and no-snapshot real-prefix restarts rest on a real leader/commit/apply prefix, and there the staged commit index lagged the last log index (8302) because the leader stages the pre-dispatch commit index.

The with-snapshot control eliminated the replay rather than shortening it, so real-prefix restarts whose replay is between 1 and 128 batches were not exercised; that recovery region is bracketed only by the seeded 9-batch case and inferred from source for the real prefix.

fsm_applied_sampled is one sample at the end of each window and was 0 in every case, including the returning controls where runFSM had not yet applied anything, so it is not used as evidence of completion.

Out of scope here: whether the installSnapshot and restoreUserSnapshot sends to the same channel can block indefinitely on a running node, where runFSM is already active and would provide backpressure rather than a permanent block.
